text: Gold bounced overnight to about $4,056 (+0.6%), recovering only part of Tuesday's 2.6% fall after the hot inflation report; later morning quotes were a little lower, near $4,044–4,050.
Silver led the rebound, up about 2.7% to near $52.92, so the gold/silver ratio dropped from 78.4 to about 76.7. SLV and AGQ have not traded since Tuesday's close.
Brent rose about 1.4% to $92.77 after Iran said tankers hit mines in the Strait of Hormuz, reversing part of Tuesday's slide on peace hopes; this matters for NRGU.
The US bond market is closed for Veterans Day while stocks trade normally, so Treasury yields stay at Tuesday's levels until Thursday.
Nasdaq 100 futures were up about 1.7% and S&P 500 futures about 0.7% early Wednesday, helped by CoreWeave jumping after raising its outlook; this matters for QQQ, TQQQ and SQQQ.
The dollar index edged up to about 102.5, near its October high, and USD/JPY held just under 159 as traders watched for Japanese intervention.
Bitcoin was little changed near $73,938, still close to a three-month low.
